# Device chains and racks evidence

## Question, route and limits

F-05 asks which rack/chain workflows can be specified from the installed package,
retained native exports and the official manual, without running Live. The
canonical proposed behavioral owner is [SPEC-DEVICE-RACKS](../specs/device-racks.md).
The [full inventory](full-live-coverage-inventory.md) identifies four rack types;
they are part of 102 overlapping device profiles, not a behavior-complete rack
inventory. [ADR 0005](../decisions/adr-0005-full-live-specification-coverage.md)
and the [coverage design](full-live-specification-design.md) require supported
transitions/cases and retain all unknowns.

Read the existing [parameter storage](../specs/bundled-device-parameters.md),
[Set structure](../specs/live-set-structure.md), [device bundles](device-bundles-static.md)
and [parameter mapping](device-parameter-mapping-native.md) before capture.
Their rack parameter binding observation (Channel 16 with a small controller
index and mapping range) remains an observed representation with unresolved
macro-index semantics; current manual prose does not trace that serialization.
This packet does not revise those clauses or expand any existing release.

## Source capture and reproducibility

All paths, sizes, hashes, capture timestamps and source versions are in
[sources.json](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/racks/sources.json).
The retained [capture script](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/racks/capture.py)
uses standard-library HTTP, HTML parsing, gzip/XML reads and JSON filtering.
Reruns reuse captured HTML, preserving its original bytes/timestamp. No package,
original code, Max patch or application was executed; no tool was installed.

| Evidence | Exact identity/locator | What it establishes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RACKS-MAN-RACKS | [Official rack chapter](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/instrument-drum-and-effect-racks/), Version 12, captured 2026-10-19T20:01:50.641719Z; SHA-256 `9b93de0730839152a58dcb843bd74ab0385b6cfa1fb6d58bb28306200ad582fb`; [HTML](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/racks/manual-racks-2026-10-19.html), [headings with exact HTML lines](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/racks/manual-racks-headings.json) | Documented chain/zones/macros/drum/pad/extraction interactions; 12.4.3 parity U |
| RACKS-MAN-DEVICES | [Official device chapter](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/working-with-instruments-and-effects/), Version 12, captured 2026-10-19T20:01:52.371400Z; SHA-256 `6a783fde3de24178e1b1d4b8431ada1a1691a1c8f16a633f909bac347e72cd82`; [HTML](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/racks/manual-devices-2026-10-19.html), [heading records](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/racks/manual-devices-headings.json) | Documented common device insertion/move/paste/activator/preset actions; 12.4.3 parity U |
| RACKS-SCHEMA | Installed `Schema/12.0_12402.txt`, 441,285 bytes; SHA-256 `b7c9d4c767d8ca9b346ce7d517265446bbacd6de366cc058e155613789d0f299`; [13-class extraction](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/racks/schema-fields.json) | Exact stored field declarations and source class lines, not runtime or accepted-file semantics |
| RACKS-DEMO | Installed Suite Demo, 3,942,573 bytes; SHA-256 `3f1c0f924b750c2adba2525838f2bc00856e52faea09d43b9279c6a0fe40952b`; [33 rack/branch records](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/racks/shipped-racks.json) | Historical examples shipped in target, Creator 12.4d1; no current save/load observation |
| RACKS-VARIATION-EXAMPLE | Installed `Core Library/Defaults/Slicing/Default.adg`; original [ADG](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/racks/variation-example.adg), [identity and five snapshot excerpts](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/racks/variation-example.json) | Snapshot value/presence representation exists in a shipped file; recall meaning not traced |
| RACKS-NATIVE-STRINGS | Retained arm64 `corpus/indexes/strings.jsonl`, 103,127,314 bytes; SHA-256 `eca2037497cf83b538a48330e974a8d1bf37048a1cf9913345aee4deef8e0f31`; [12 exact line/hash/ref records](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/racks/native-strings.json) | Names and references only; no caller sequence, execution or behavioral proof |

The installed-source identity remains [SRC-ABLETON-12-4-3](sources/ableton-live-12.4.3.md).
The Suite Demo is a different source from the Intro Demo used in the inventory;
its bytes/hash and rack counts must not be substituted for the Intro capture.
The original schema is retained by the existing inventory; this packet stores
excerpts and its hash rather than making a second source revision.

## Observations and interpretation

**Observed, installed schema.** Four rack classes each expose sixteen macros,
visibility state, randomization/snapshot exclusions and variation state. The
ZoneRange class declares Min, Max, CrossfadeMin and CrossfadeMax; ZoneSettings
contains key and velocity ranges. Instrument/MIDI branches reference
ZoneSettings. DrumBranch references BranchInfo of class DrumZoneSettings, which
contains ReceivingNote, SendingNote and ChokeGroup. MacroSnapshot has sixteen
MacroValues and sixteen MacroHasValue fields; MacroVariations holds a snapshot
list. Exact lines and declarations live in the extraction above. These names
are analyst evidence, not a candidate implementation prescription.

**Observed, shipped documents.** The retained Suite Demo has 23 audio-effect,
one MIDI-effect, eight instrument and one drum rack elements (nested elements
count individually). The first instrument and MIDI-effect branch examples
store key bounds 0..127, velocity 1..127, selector 0..0. The demo has no
MacroSnapshot entries. A separately retained slicing default has five. Both
files identify Creator 12.4d1 with MinorVersion 12.0_12402, so they demonstrate
historical shipped representations. They are not fresh 12.4.3 outputs.

**Documented, Version 12.** The official rack chapter provides concrete semantic
rules absent from the schema. The spec separates key/velocity filtering,
selector filtering, velocity versus output-audio fades, and the treatment of
existing tails with/without selector fades. It also distinguishes a pad's note
identity from chain identity, Receive All Notes from a single note, and drum
chain extraction through the Session mixer from extraction through the chain
list. Macro randomization exclusions and variation exclusions are independent
controls. No random distribution or sample-level audio rule is supplied by the
chapter. All runtime clauses therefore retain exact-build applicability U.

**Inferred, deliberately not promoted.** Matching schema/field names and manual
titles suggest that documented workflows concern present surfaces. This is
presence corroboration only. In particular DrumBranch stores a selector range
although the manual says Drum Racks have no zones. That is not a contradiction:
file field presence does not prove an exposed editor or active filter. No Drum
selector semantic was invented from that shared storage.

## Case and claim boundary

The draft contains 28 requirements and [61 authored cases](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/racks/cases.json):
3 installed-source assertions, 46 criteria gradeable only in the documented
Version 12 domain, and 12 ungraded U experiments. None ran against Live or a
candidate; all runtime comparisons keep target-build parity U. Cases separate
positive, negative, boundary, malformed, cancellation and teardown scenarios.
Their literal inputs and comparator scope are retained in JSON; the table in
the spec remains the canonical human-readable contract.

Unsupported outcomes include exact fades/summation, note-off/sustain handling,
MPE and simultaneous choke arbitration, macro range interpolation and binding
encoding, random distribution, selector/recall scheduling, latency/CPU behavior,
resource limits, failed-load atomicity, shared-note extraction, nested mapping
preservation, undo grouping, migration and rack-specific malformed-file repair.
A device activator's documented “unprocessed” description is narrowed to a
qualitative audio-effect bypass criterion; the instrument's MIDI-to-audio case
stays U. Esc exits Hot-Swap but is not asserted to roll back a loaded preset.
The current manual's A/B device-state subsection and broader defaults behavior
need separate applicability/ownership work and are not covered here.

## Review packet and downstream work

The first independent review requested two source/fixture corrections, RR-01
and RR-02. Direct parsing of the retained HTML confirmed that multiple mappings
reset the generic macro name independently of the units exception, and that
custom defaults/presets can change initial rack state. REQ-013 and RCK-026 now
separate same-unit/range and different-unit outcomes. REQ-011/RCK-023 require
factory rack creation without custom defaults/presets; REQ-014/RCK-028 require
an unmodified factory Instrument Rack preset without an exclusion override.
Counts remain 28 requirements and 61 cases. The original author seal is retained
as [manifest-author-r1.json](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/racks/manifest-author-r1.json);
the current seal includes these corrections and awaits a focused recheck.

[Manifest](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/racks/manifest.json)
freezes the author packet, including exact page hashes. Independent review must
check claim/source alignment, case counts, platform modifiers and all exclusions.
No rack profile is complete, no release was modified and no host-protocol gap
was closed. The root coordinator owns catalog, coverage, questions and log
integration. [Q-027](../questions.md#q-027-whole-product-specification-evidence-and-version-coverage)
tracks whole-product evidence/version applicability;
[Q-025](../questions.md#q-025-device-host-protocol-and-device-audio-acceptance)
retains host/mapping gaps. Amp/Cabinet host emulation remains blocked and T1.6
remains pending; neither was needed for this read-only documentary packet.

# Device chains and racks

## Scope and authority

This partial draft owns FEAT-RACKS and selected common FEAT-DEVICES workflows:
four rack types, parallel chains, zones, macros, variations, drum mapping,
returns, pad editing and extraction. It adds common device insertion, bypass and
preset interactions where they explain rack use. It does not specify the sound
of contained devices or the plug-in host API. The four rack profiles in the
[full inventory](../research/full-live-coverage-inventory.md) are discovery entries,
not four completed behavioral contracts.

The [Live Set structure](live-set-structure.md) owns device-list storage, generic
reader validation and identifiers. [Bundled device parameters](bundled-device-parameters.md)
owns the seven bundles' parameter values and its unresolved macro binding encoding.
[Automation](automation-envelopes.md), [mixer values](mixer-values.md) and
[mix graph](mix-graph.md) retain their existing scope; none implies that every
rack mutation, mixer operation or load is already specified. Browser navigation
belongs to [browser workflows](browser-workflows.md).

**D12** means documented in the retained official Version 12 manual captured
2026-10-19. Every D12 runtime clause has **exact-build applicability U**, even
when a schema name corroborates the feature. **D-installed** means bytes in the
pinned installed package; it specifies a documentary observation only.
**U** means no gradeable expected outcome. No reference application, original
function or candidate was executed for this packet. Nothing here is released.
Evidence keys E1–E5 resolve in the analysis-only appendix.

## Preconditions and observable state

Use a valid, editable Set; readable named samples and devices; an audio path for
audible cases; and MIDI input or clips for note cases. Reset mappings, zones,
selection, sends and exclusions to the values stated in each case. Factory
sample-dropping defaults are required where the case expects Simpler; custom
pad/default presets are a separate source of variation. Disable unrelated
randomization, automation and MIDI processing unless named. Tests of a tail use
a contained effect known independently to produce a tail. They establish rack
routing/attenuation qualitatively, never its samples or gain curve.

Track/chain membership and order, note-to-chain assignment, selection/focus,
macro values/mappings/exclusions, snapshots, send/return destinations and pad
presentation are separate observable state. Cases below compare only named
state and events. No deadline, audio tolerance, MIDI-event ordering or undo
transaction is implied by “immediate” presentation or parallel routing.

## Requirements

### REQ-DEVICE-RACKS-001 — installed vocabulary and examples

**D-installed / E3–E5.** The installed schema declares Audio Effect, MIDI Effect,
Instrument and Drum rack classes. Each declares sixteen macro control fields,
visibility count, randomization and snapshot exclusions, a chain list and macro
variations. ZoneRange declares minimum, maximum and two crossfade bounds;
MacroSnapshot declares sixteen values and sixteen presence flags. The retained
Suite demo contains respectively 23, 1, 8 and 1 rack occurrences. The retained
slicing preset contains five snapshots. These are documentary assertions, not
load/save or semantic rules for the private field names. In particular the Drum
branch's stored selector range does **not** establish a Drum Rack zone editor.

### REQ-DEVICE-RACKS-002 — rack type and legal signal placement

**D12 / E1 §25.2.** MIDI Effect Racks hold MIDI effects on MIDI tracks. Audio Effect
Racks hold audio effects on audio paths, including after an instrument on a MIDI
track. Instrument and Drum chains order MIDI effects before an instrument and
audio effects after it. Invalid placement is outside the documented valid
configuration; exact drag rejection, relocation, replacement and malformed-file
responses are U. This does not resolve the file-reader question in
REQ-LIVE-SET-STRUCTURE-012.

### REQ-DEVICE-RACKS-003 — serial, parallel and nested flow

**D12 / E1 §25.1.1.** Devices within a chain process left to right. Instrument and
effect rack chains receive the same input in parallel subject to their zones;
their outputs combine at the rack output, then feed downstream devices. Drum
chains receive assigned notes instead (REQ-016). A rack may contain racks and
acts as a device in the enclosing chain. Exact summation, ordering of coincident
MIDI events, latency and maximum practical nesting depth are U.

### REQ-DEVICE-RACKS-004 — creation, grouping and dismantling

**D12 / E1 §25.2.** Loading a generic rack creates an empty rack. Group selected
devices, Group to Drum Rack and grouping existing chains create enclosing racks;
repeated grouping can nest them. Selecting a rack title and Ungroup dismantles
that rack. The manual does not define flattening/routing resolution for every
multi-chain or return-containing rack; those outcomes are U.

### REQ-DEVICE-RACKS-005 — chain list and selection

**D12 / E1 §§25.3–25.4.1.** Dropping devices, presets or chains in the chain-list
drop area adds chains. Selecting a chain shows its devices; multiple selections
show their count. Chains expose activator, solo and hot-swap; audio-output rack
chains also expose volume/pan. Rack-title selection addresses the whole rack for
move/copy/delete. Auto Select selects chains currently processing signals;
Drum Rack selection follows receipt of the assigned note. Exact solo/activator
audio interaction, selection expiry and contention with manual selection are U.

### REQ-DEVICE-RACKS-006 — available zone filters

**D12 / E1 §§25.5–25.5.1.** Instrument and MIDI Effect Racks have key, velocity and
selector zones; a note enters a chain only if it passes all three. Audio Effect
Racks have selector zones, without MIDI key/velocity zones. Drum Racks have no
zone editor; their Receive choosers filter notes. All matching parallel chains
can receive the same qualifying input.

### REQ-DEVICE-RACKS-007 — zone editing and ranges

**D12 / E1 §§25.5–25.5.4.1.** Zones can be moved and resized, with separately
editable fades. Key zones cover selected MIDI keys; velocity zones use Note On
velocities 1–127. The selector scale is 0–127; the documented initial selector
zone is the single value 0. Multiple chains may share ranges. Exact rounding,
edge inclusion for resized ranges, out-of-range edits and MIDI velocity-zero
interpretation are U here; note encoding belongs to [MIDI note storage](midi-note-storage.md).

### REQ-DEVICE-RACKS-008 — fade destination

**D12 / E1 §§25.5.2–25.5.4.** Key/velocity fades attenuate incoming note velocity.
Selector fades in a MIDI Effect Rack attenuate note velocity. Selector fades in
Instrument and Audio Effect Racks attenuate chain output audio. Exact fade law,
rounding to MIDI velocity, overlap normalization and treatment of a zero-length
fade are U; no linear or equal-power equation is specified.

### REQ-DEVICE-RACKS-009 — selector filtering of controllers

**D12 / E1 §25.5.4.** Instrument and MIDI Effect Rack selector zones filter notes
by default, allowing other MIDI events such as controllers through. Enabling
Chain Selector Filters MIDI Ctrl makes the selector filter all MIDI events.
Held-note release routing and sustain/channel-mode edge cases remain U.

### REQ-DEVICE-RACKS-010 — selector movement and existing tails

**D12 / E1 §25.5.4.** For an audio-output chain with a fade ending its selector
zone, moving outside attenuates the output to zero. With no fade, leaving the
selector zone does not attenuate existing output; an existing effect tail may
finish according to that effect. This distinction does not specify audio effect
input admission, voice lifetime, clicks, smoothing or compensation changes.

### REQ-DEVICE-RACKS-011 — macro count and visibility

**D12 / E1 §25.7; E2 §§23.2.3,23.2.6.1.** A rack supports up to sixteen macros;
a newly created factory rack, with no custom default or loaded preset, shows
eight. Visibility controls change the number shown; shown/hidden state is
saved with the Set. Hidden-control mapping activity and lower visibility bound
are U. E3 corroborates sixteen storage slots, without proving runtime limits.

### REQ-DEVICE-RACKS-012 — mapping and ranges

**D12 / E1 §25.7.1.** Entering Macro Map Mode highlights mappable controls, shows
macro Map buttons and opens the Mapping Browser. Select a contained parameter,
then a macro's Map button to create an assignment; one macro can address several
parameters. Min/Max refine each assignment; Min greater than Max inverts it,
and Invert Range reverses the current range. Assignments can be edited/deleted
in that browser; leaving Map Mode ends this editing mode. Exact interpolation,
quantized parameters and out-of-domain mappings are U.

### REQ-DEVICE-RACKS-013 — delegated control and macro display

**D12 / E1 §25.7.1.** A mapped device parameter is disabled for direct control;
clip-envelope modulation remains possible. A single mapping supplies its name
and units to the macro by default. Multiple mappings restore the generic macro
name regardless of whether their units match, absent a separately applied
custom name. Multiple mappings use 0–127 units unless every target has the same
unit type and range; in that case, the common units and range are retained.
Custom names/colors/info text are editable. Restored values after unmapping and
interactions with automation override are U.

### REQ-DEVICE-RACKS-014 — randomization and exclusions

**D12 / E1 §25.7.2.** Rand randomizes mapped macros. Exclude Macro from
Randomization preserves an excluded mapped control. Macros assigned to Volume
parameters in unmodified factory Instrument Rack presets, without a user
exclusion override, are excluded by default. This last clause
does not assert an automatic exclusion after every new volume mapping.
Distribution, seed, correlation, repeatability, unchanged-value probability,
hidden/unmapped controls and randomization undo granularity are U.

### REQ-DEVICE-RACKS-015 — variations

**D12 / E1 §25.7.3.** New stores current macro state as a variation, initially
named sequentially Variation 1, Variation 2, and so on. Variations can be
renamed, duplicated and deleted. Launch recalls a stored state; Overwrite
replaces it with the current state. Exclude Macro From Variations prevents that
control changing on launch; disabling the exclusion restores participation.
Snapshot behavior during mapping changes, which unmapped values are present,
parameter automation ownership, launch scheduling and interpolation are U.

### REQ-DEVICE-RACKS-016 — drum receive, play and choke

**D12 / E1 §25.6.** Receive selects the note triggering a drum chain; Play selects
the outgoing note delivered to its devices. Chains assigned the same one of
sixteen choke groups silence one another when triggered. Receive All Notes
disables Play/Choke and passes through the received note. Preview fires a note
into a chain. Choke release envelopes, exact stop time, same-sample arbitration,
self-choke and preview velocity are U.

### REQ-DEVICE-RACKS-017 — drum sends and returns

**D12 / E1 §§25.2,25.6.** Drum Racks have up to six audio-effect return chains.
Drum-chain sends feed them after the drum chain's fader; send controls require
at least one return chain. Each return's Audio To can target the rack output or
a Set return track. A seventh return's UI/error behavior, return feedback,
missing destinations, send scaling and compensation are U.

### REQ-DEVICE-RACKS-018 — dropping onto pads

**D12 / E1 §25.6.1.** Each pad denotes a MIDI note. With factory dropping defaults,
a sample on an empty pad creates a chain with Simpler. Dropping an audio effect
on that pad adds it after the instrument. A replacement sample replaces the
Simpler/sample and preserves upstream MIDI and downstream audio effects.
Custom dropping defaults are outside this clause; failed-load atomicity is U.

### REQ-DEVICE-RACKS-019 — pad distribution, swapping and layering

**D12 / E1 §25.6.1.** Multiple samples dropped normally populate chromatically
upward from the destination, replacing samples while preserving effects.
Alt-drag on Windows / Cmd-drag on macOS layers them in a nested Instrument Rack.
Dragging a pad to another swaps note assignments; existing clips keep their
notes and therefore address the new sounds. The same platform modifier layers
both pads' chains in a nested Instrument Rack. Overflow above note 127, sample
ordering within a multiselection and effects during failed loads are U.

### REQ-DEVICE-RACKS-020 — pads represent notes, including multiple chains

**D12 / E1 §25.6.1.** The 128-note pad map shows groups of sixteen. Changing Receive
updates pad presentation; matching chains, including nested ones, respond to
the note. A one-chain pad shows that chain's name and permits rename/hot-swap.
A multiple-chain pad displays Multi; mute/solo/preview address all its chains,
rename/hot-swap are disabled, and delete removes all those chains. Exact mixed
mute/solo icon semantics and controller scrolling protocols are U.

### REQ-DEVICE-RACKS-021 — rack mixing in Session

**D12 / E1 §25.8.** Instrument/Drum racks with multiple chains can unfold into the
Session mixer. Chains have no clip slots. Their controls mirror the rack list;
selecting a chain's mixer title shows its devices. Multiselected Session chains
share a mixer parameter adjustment; the same adjustment from the rack chain
list does not invoke this multi-chain behavior. Relative scaling/clamping of
unequal starting values is U.

### REQ-DEVICE-RACKS-022 — extracting chains

**D12 / E1 §25.8.1.** Chains can be moved to other racks/tracks. Dragging a drum
chain from the Session mixer to a new track transfers its devices and MIDI
notes. Dragging from the chain list transfers devices only. Dragging a drum
return to the mixer creates a return track. The exact treatment of shared-note
chains, nested mappings, clip ownership, automation, sends and source empty
clips is U; no broad preservation/undo promise is implied.

### REQ-DEVICE-RACKS-023 — inserting common devices

**D12 / E2 §§23,23.2.** Double-clicking a browser device targets the selected track
or creates a track if none is selected. Enter loads a selected device/preset on
a selected destination track. Devices can be dragged into track/device views;
sample drop on an empty MIDI Device View creates Simpler. Chains follow MIDI
effects → instrument → audio effects and process left to right. Exact
insertion position with existing selection and incompatible-device handling
are U beyond the explicit paste rule below.

### REQ-DEVICE-RACKS-024 — move, remove and paste

**D12 / E2 §23.2.** Device title selection and Delete/Backspace removes the device;
dragging its title reorders or moves it between tracks. Cut/copy/paste/duplicate
apply to devices. Paste inserts before the selected device; selecting the empty
space after the last device permits paste at the end. Rack title selection
addresses its whole contents (REQ-005). No audio continuity or retained-tail
guarantee follows from the manual's qualified continuity statement.

### REQ-DEVICE-RACKS-025 — activator bypass

**D12 / E2 §23.2.1.** The activator turns a device on/off; the manual describes an
off device as leaving the signal unprocessed. For an audio effect this provides
a qualitative bypass requirement. It does not establish sample equality,
latency changes, tail retention, CPU counters, retained processor state or the
meaning of unprocessed MIDI at a disabled instrument's audio output; those
outcomes remain U.

### REQ-DEVICE-RACKS-026 — presets and hot-swap

**D12 / E2 §§23.2.3–23.2.5.** Devices/racks can save settings as presets. Save Preset
opens the browser with a prospective name; Enter confirms and Esc cancels the
save process. Dragging a device title into a Places folder is another save
route. Hot-Swap connects a target with the browser, and only compatible device
types can be swapped. Q, Esc or the close controls exit Hot-Swap; exit alone is
not documented as restoring an earlier loaded preset. Overwrite/cancel disk
atomicity, media collection, failed loads and custom-default precedence require
separate evidence. Current-manual A/B device states and newer defaults are not
silently included in this bounded contract.

### REQ-DEVICE-RACKS-027 — malformed state, cancellation and teardown

**U / E1–E5 limits.** For malformed zone bounds, illegal note/choke/return values,
missing/duplicate snapshot members, cancelled pad/extract/mapping operations,
held notes while deleting/unmapping/choking, lost media or closing during load,
no rack-specific refusal, repair, rollback, cleanup or timing outcome has been
established. Generic file parsing remains owned by the container/structure
specifications; their checks do not prove rack-specific semantic validation.

### REQ-DEVICE-RACKS-028 — persistence, automation, undo and timing

**U except REQ-011's D12 visibility persistence.** Exact 12.4.3 reopen preservation
of mappings, zones, variants, exclusions, routing and nested references; migration;
undo/redo grouping; automation/clip modulation precedence across maps and recalls;
note-off/sustain routing across selector changes; transport/scheduler order;
latency/CPU behavior and sample-exact output remain unresolved. Schemas and
examples establish representations, not accepted-input or runtime laws.

## Acceptance cases

[Cases JSON](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/racks/cases.json)
retains the same authored cases as this table. **I** cases grade only installed
source assertions. **D** cases have a documented-domain expected comparator,
with exact 12.4.3 applicability U. **U** cases are ungraded experiments with no
invented expectation. All execution results are unexecuted; “graded” describes
available criteria, not a test result. Numbers in the requirement column use
the REQ-DEVICE-RACKS prefix. State-only checks require exact equality of named
fields; event checks compare note/controller admission, without timing or event
order. No case is an original-versus-candidate compatibility pass.

| Case | Req | Kind/domain | Setup and action | Expected comparator or open result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RCK-001 | 001 | Boundary/I | Parse E3 four rack classes, ZoneRange and MacroSnapshot. | Exactly sixteen macro slots and snapshot values/presence flags; four zone bounds. |
| RCK-002 | 001 | Positive/I | Reparse E4 Suite demo and count rack elements. | Audio 23, MIDI 1, Instrument 8, Drum 1; Creator 12.4d1. |
| RCK-003 | 001 | Positive/I | Decode E5 slicing ADG. | Five MacroSnapshot entries; record their stored value/presence fields without recall inference. |
| RCK-004 | 002 | Positive/D | Put a MIDI effect in a MIDI Effect Rack on a MIDI track. | Valid documented signal configuration. |
| RCK-005 | 002,027 | Negative/U | Drag an instrument into an audio-only rack, then load equivalent malformed XML. | U: refusal vs relocation/replacement and UI/load differences. |
| RCK-006 | 002,003 | Positive/D | Instrument chain: MIDI effect, instrument, audio effect. | MIDI processing precedes synthesis; audio effect follows it. |
| RCK-007 | 003 | Positive/D | Rack with two distinct active chains receiving a qualifying note. | Both chains receive the note; outputs feed the enclosing downstream chain. |

# Plug-in hosting workflows

## Scope and authority

This partial analyst contract owns third-party plug-in placement, parameter-panel
configuration, editors, selected sidechain and program workflows. It complements
[discovery](plugin-discovery.md), [racks/common device actions](device-racks.md)
and [bundled-device hosting](bundled-device-hosting.md). Scanner isolation is not
instantiation isolation. Engine compensation/routing and full plug-in API behavior
remain separate obligations; no API/callback architecture is prescribed.

D12 means a predicate supported by captured Version 12 documentation; its
applicability to exact 12.4.3 is unknown throughout. No original or candidate
application, plug-in, editor or codec was executed. No fixture binary is supplied.
Presence or format support is not proof of arbitrary vendor compatibility.
Sources and limitations belong to [the research owner](../research/plugin-hosting.md).

## Inputs, state and observable outcomes

Inputs are format/role/capabilities, track placement, published parameter identity,
panel and editor state, window preferences, mappings/envelopes, program selection,
files and routing. Observe panel membership/order, warnings, editor visibility and
parameter state, Set-restored configuration and file-dialog operation. Do not
substitute internal callback logs for an app-observable requirement. Discrete
membership/order predicates have no numerical tolerance; all audio/timing/rounding
oracles remain U unless explicitly retained from a later evidence packet.

## Requirements

### REQ-PLUGIN-HOSTING-001 — Placement and formats

**D12; exact-build U.** VST2/VST3 and macOS AU2/AU3 are documented formats. Instruments accept MIDI and output audio on MIDI tracks; effects belong on audio tracks or after instruments. Format availability does not prove any particular plug-in compatible. [Source using-plug-ins](#source-using-plug-ins).

### REQ-PLUGIN-HOSTING-002 — Initial parameter panel

**D12; exact-build U.** For an unconfigured instance with no overriding default, a plug-in with at most 64 modifiable parameters exposes them in the Live panel; above 64 the initial panel is empty. Parameter enumeration/filtering and hidden/read-only parameter counting remain U. [Source plug-ins-in-the-device-view](#source-plug-ins-in-the-device-view).

### REQ-PLUGIN-HOSTING-003 — Panel visibility and X-Y assignments

**D12; exact-build U.** The title-bar unfold control shows/hides the panel. Two choosers assign parameters to the X-Y field. Numeric X-Y interpolation, automation and coupled parameter writes remain U. [Source plug-ins-in-the-device-view](#source-plug-ins-in-the-device-view).

### REQ-PLUGIN-HOSTING-004 — Floating editor correspondence

**D12; exact-build U.** Show/Hide Plug-In Window opens the original plug-in editor; an exposed parameter can be changed from either editor or Live panel with the same parameter effect. Update timing/rounding/threading and unsupported editors remain U. [Source showing-plug-in-panels-in-separate-windows](#source-showing-plug-in-panels-in-separate-windows).

### REQ-PLUGIN-HOSTING-005 — Window preferences

**D12; exact-build U.** Auto-Open opens editors for browser-loaded devices. Multiple Plug-In Windows allows concurrent editors; with it off, Ctrl on Windows or Cmd on Mac while opening preserves previous windows. Auto-Hide limits displayed editors to the selected track. Option interactions and restoration order remain U. [Source showing-plug-in-panels-in-separate-windows](#source-showing-plug-in-panels-in-separate-windows).

### REQ-PLUGIN-HOSTING-006 — Global editor visibility

**D12; exact-build U.** The View command or Ctrl-Alt-P on Windows / Cmd-Option-P on Mac toggles already-open editors; the shortcut requires prior manual opening or Auto-Open enabled. A visible editor title identifies its track. Exact geometry, focus, resize and accessibility remain U. [Source showing-plug-in-panels-in-separate-windows](#source-showing-plug-in-panels-in-separate-windows).

### REQ-PLUGIN-HOSTING-007 — Configure admission

**D12; exact-build U.** Configure adds published parameters by clicking them in the original editor, with an actual value change required by some plug-ins. Unpublished parameters cannot be added. A click-only failure is not a host failure unless that plug-in publishes by click. [Source plug-in-configure-mode](#source-plug-in-configure-mode).

### REQ-PLUGIN-HOSTING-008 — Configure reorder and deletion warning

**D12; exact-build U.** In Configure, displayed parameters can be reordered by drag and removed with Delete. Existing automation, clip envelopes, MIDI/key/Macro mappings trigger a warning before deletion. Warning choices, cancellation side effects and data survival after confirmation remain U. [Source plug-in-configure-mode](#source-plug-in-configure-mode).

### REQ-PLUGIN-HOSTING-009 — Instances and persistence

**D12; exact-build U.** Configured parameter lists belong to individual instances and are saved in the Set. A configured device can be retained in a saved rack or configuration default. Plug-in DSP state, missing binaries, default precedence and exact saved representation remain U; generic rack/default actions route to SPEC-DEVICE-RACKS. [Source plug-in-configure-mode](#source-plug-in-configure-mode).

### REQ-PLUGIN-HOSTING-010 — Editorless plug-ins

**D12; exact-build U.** For a plug-in without its own window, Configure permits reordering but not deleting its Live-panel parameters. Editor creation/teardown failure is a separate U condition. [Source plug-in-configure-mode](#source-plug-in-configure-mode).

### REQ-PLUGIN-HOSTING-011 — Temporary parameter entries

**D12; exact-build U.** Changing a parameter in the floating editor creates temporary automation/clip-envelope/X-Y chooser entries, removed when another parameter is adjusted. Editing its envelope, selecting another parameter in the envelope chooser, or selecting it in an X-Y chooser makes the entry permanent. Duplicate handling, visibility order and interrupted changes remain U. [Source plug-in-configure-mode](#source-plug-in-configure-mode).

### REQ-PLUGIN-HOSTING-012 — Recording and mapping additions

**D12; exact-build U.** Changing editor parameters during recording records automation and adds the automated parameters to the panel when recording stops. In MIDI/key/Macro mapping mode, adjusting an editor parameter creates and selects its panel entry. Recording prerequisites, envelope values and mapping transforms remain with their canonical owners or U. [Source plug-in-configure-mode](#source-plug-in-configure-mode).

### REQ-PLUGIN-HOSTING-013 — Sidechain source and endpoints

**D12; exact-build U.** A supporting plug-in can choose an internal routing point as trigger. Gain affects this trigger, not source mix volume; Mix=100% uses only the sidechain and Mix=0% bypasses the sidechain trigger. Intermediate mixing law, channel conversion, latency and plug-in response remain U. [Source sidechain-parameters](#source-sidechain-parameters).

### REQ-PLUGIN-HOSTING-014 — Sidechain Mute control

**D12; exact-build U.** The documented Mute permits auditioning the plug-in output while bypassing the sidechain source input. The exact affected routing branch and interactions with independent source monitoring/sends remain U; no global track-mute law is inferred. [Source sidechain-parameters](#source-sidechain-parameters).

### REQ-PLUGIN-HOSTING-015 — VST programs and files

**D12; exact-build U.** The selected VST program belongs to its instance; edits affect that program. The chooser selects programs; Rename Plug-In Preset renames the current one. Load accepts a program or bank; Save can target the current program or bank via the format choice. VST2/VST3 per-format applicability, binary formats and failure/atomicity remain U. [Source vst-presets-and-banks](#source-vst-presets-and-banks).

### REQ-PLUGIN-HOSTING-016 — Audio Units distinctions

**D12; exact-build U.** AU is macOS-only. Some modes are accessible only through the original editor. Some AU presets are read-only and cannot be dragged elsewhere; documented preset storage is under the user Library Audio/Presets manufacturer/plug-in path. Actual extension spelling/encoding, AU2/AU3 differences and exact permissions/failure results remain U. [Source audio-units-plug-ins](#source-audio-units-plug-ins).

### REQ-PLUGIN-HOSTING-017 — Processing and timing

**U; exact-build U.** No host processing-block, MIDI/event schedule, automation delivery, channel layout, latency notification, bypass/tail, render or dropout oracle is established here. Discovery/placement/UI presence does not prove processing compatibility. [Source plug-in-configure-mode](#source-plug-in-configure-mode).

### REQ-PLUGIN-HOSTING-018 — Opaque state and identity

**U; exact-build U.** State restore, vendor version/format substitution, duplicate identifiers, missing/disabled plug-ins, reopening and unavailable plug-in recovery remain unknown beyond the configured-panel documentary clause. [Source plug-in-configure-mode](#source-plug-in-configure-mode).

### REQ-PLUGIN-HOSTING-019 — Malformed data and faults

**U; exact-build U.** Malformed program/bank/state, instantiation failure, editor crash/hang and invalid plug-in responses have no established application outcome. Scanner fault behavior remains owned by SPEC-PLUGIN-DISCOVERY and is not imported as instantiation isolation. [Source vst-presets-and-banks](#source-vst-presets-and-banks).

### REQ-PLUGIN-HOSTING-020 — Cancel undo and teardown

**U; exact-build U.** Cancel of configuration warnings or file dialogs, undo/redo of parameter-list/device operations and removal/Set-close with editors, automation or active notes remain unknown. No leak/crash/focus/tail criterion is invented. [Source plug-in-configure-mode](#source-plug-in-configure-mode).

### REQ-PLUGIN-HOSTING-021 — Multi-I/O and remote control integration

**D12; exact-build U.** Panel parameters can be MIDI-mapped; continuous parameters accept clip envelopes; supporting plug-ins can participate in track I/O routing and accept custom info text. Exact port selection, event routing, envelope laws and text persistence remain with existing owners or U. [Source plug-in-configure-mode](#source-plug-in-configure-mode).

# Sets, projects and media-reference workflows

## Scope and authority

FEAT-PERSISTENCE and FEAT-PROJECT-MANAGEMENT. User tasks: create/save and merge
Sets, use templates, inspect/repair/collect referenced assets, manage unused
files and create/restore project Packs. This is a partial documented-domain
contract. The current official Live 12 chapter was captured 2026-10-19; it names
no exact patch revision. **Every D12 behavioral clause retains exact 12.4.3
applicability U.** No original program, candidate, codec, project mutation or
file-operation acceptance scenario was executed.

[ALS container](als-container.md) owns the file envelope/version checks;
[Live Set structure](live-set-structure.md) owns its existing reader subset;
[browser index](browser-index.md) owns indexed content/sidecars and
[browser workflows](browser-workflows.md) owns search/navigation. This page owns
user-facing project/media lifecycle, not a replacement serializer or dependency
resolution algorithm. [Arrangement editing](arrangement-editing.md) owns edit
transactions still unknown there; generic Undo History presentation below does
not establish any particular edit's undo grouping or rollback behavior.

D12 = documented in the retained chapter, with target-build parity U. U = no
supported outcome. Requirement suffixes refer to this page's REQ prefix. Source
keys E1–E14 resolve to exact HTML anchors in the appendix. Concrete scenarios
are authored definitions, not original-side captures or ready-made ALS files.

## Preconditions and state

Use fresh, valid, editable Sets and explicitly identified test projects. Reset
preferences and open Set state between cases. Sources are readable unless a
case changes that property. Set names, active project, referenced logical asset,
missing/online status, selected dependency-location classes, template contents
and Undo History are separate observable state. Compare named state only;
never assume filename identity proves equal content.

Use copies of test-owned assets for replace/delete/collect operations. This is
a fixture isolation requirement, not a claimed Live safety feature. No broad
unchanged-file/hash/atomicity guarantee follows from a successful UI operation.
Runtime-dependent failures, overwrite prompts and partially completed writes
remain U unless a requirement explicitly says otherwise.

## Requirements

| Requirement ID | Preconditions/input | Observable documentary result | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| REQ-PROJECT-MEDIA-001 | New/Open/Open Recent or browser Set open | Create or open the selected Set through the named command. | D12/E1 |
| REQ-PROJECT-MEDIA-002 | Save current Set; Save As; Save a Copy | Save current content; the latter commands support a different name/location. Active-document identity after Save a Copy remains U here. | D12/E1 |
| REQ-PROJECT-MEDIA-003 | Open Undo History for an editable Set | Actions appear newest first; selecting an earlier action undoes later actions, which become dimmed; selecting an undone action reapplies it and intervening earlier undone actions. | D12/E2 |
| REQ-PROJECT-MEDIA-004 | Close and reopen a Set | Undo History starts afresh; creating/opening is its initial non-undoable action. | D12/E2 |
| REQ-PROJECT-MEDIA-005 | Drag a source Set onto a track header/drop area | Reconstruct its tracks, Session/Arrangement clips, devices and automation, excluding source return tracks. Specific routing/ID/collision transformations U. | D12/E3 |
| REQ-PROJECT-MEDIA-006 | Unfold a source Set in browser | Expose individual tracks, nested groups, devices, grooves and Session clips for the documented selective import actions. | D12/E3 |
| REQ-PROJECT-MEDIA-007 | Drag selected Session clips into Current Project/user folder | Export a newly named Set containing that selection. Other retained content/defaults and file-reference transforms U. | D12/E4 |
| REQ-PROJECT-MEDIA-008 | Save current Set as default | New Sets use its configured state; a browser template can also be chosen as default. | D12/E5 |
| REQ-PROJECT-MEDIA-009 | Save Set as Template, then load it | List template in Templates/User Library; load its configuration as an untitled Set. | D12/E5 |
| REQ-PROJECT-MEDIA-010 | Manage Files → Manage Set → View Files | List referenced files and expandable usages; indicate missing/User Library/Project/external location. | D12/E6 |
| REQ-PROJECT-MEDIA-011 | Replace an entry with a readable new sample | Redirect every Set clip using that sample. For audio clips retain clip properties and retain Warp Markers when replacement length is at least original, discard when shorter. | D12/E6 |
| REQ-PROJECT-MEDIA-012 | Edit a referenced sample externally | Keep it offline while Edit is engaged; retain audio-clip Warp Markers only when sample length is unchanged. Non-sample Edit availability and external-editor failures U. | D12/E6 |
| REQ-PROJECT-MEDIA-013 | Save outside existing projects versus within one | Outside creates a new project; within an existing project shares that project. Save As alone does not collect external samples. | D12/E7 |
| REQ-PROJECT-MEDIA-014 | Open an older-major-version Set and try ordinary overwrite | Require Save As instead of overwriting it. Exact accepted versions remain owned by the container spec. | D12/E7 |
| REQ-PROJECT-MEDIA-015 | Referenced sample unavailable | Mark affected clip/instrument sample slot offline and substitute silence for that sample; effect/instrument tails and whole-mix silence are not implied. | D12/E8 |
| REQ-PROJECT-MEDIA-016 | Drop a readable candidate on a missing reference | Accept manual reassignment without proving it is the original missing file. Compatibility/type rejection and saved-path rules U. | D12/E9 |
| REQ-PROJECT-MEDIA-017 | Automatic search over explicitly enabled locations | No candidate: unresolved; one: accept; several: offer user selection via Hot-Swap. Matching/ranking/tie identity and search timing U. | D12/E10 |
| REQ-PROJECT-MEDIA-018 | Collect and Save selected external-location classes | Copy selected dependencies into project Samples or Presets and use project-contained references. Include files outside project, even those in Packs/User Library/other projects, as external. | D12/E11 |
| REQ-PROJECT-MEDIA-019 | Move/save a clip, preset or track from an open Set into a supported Places folder, with collection preference | Always copies; Never keeps original references; Ask offers Copy/Don't Copy/Cancel. Filename confirmation precedes dependent copying in the documented Ask/Copy path. Partial writes and cancel atomicity U. | D12/E12 |
| REQ-PROJECT-MEDIA-020 | Find unused project files | Judge use by that project's Sets/clips/presets, even when another project uses the file. Deletion can break those other references; no global safe-delete guarantee. | D12/E13 |
| REQ-PROJECT-MEDIA-021 | Create project Pack; install it later | Write an ALP without automatically collecting external files; restore the packed project folder on install. Original project remains available. Compression ratio/bytes/version safety U. | D12/E14 |
| REQ-PROJECT-MEDIA-022 | Malformed media/project, permission/disk/network failure, cancel or teardown | U: precise refusal/repair, diagnostics, overwrite decisions, partial output, transaction recovery, cleanup, undo grouping and stale references. | U |

## Timing and interactions

No file-operation deadlines, audio substitution latency, search completeness
bound, deterministic candidate ranking or total transaction order is specified.
Equal versus shorter replacement lengths are observable media-duration conditions;
no tolerance or rounding rule for almost-equal durations is invented. File-byte
interchange still requires the existing container/structure contracts and their
explicit gaps; these UI rules cannot approve arbitrary malformed ALS or ALP input.

Collecting and packing are distinct: a Pack's creation does not resolve omitted
external dependencies. A template is not a saved undo history. Changing every
reference to a sample can affect multiple clips; no per-clip replacement promise
is inferred. A stopped/cancelled operation need not imply rolled-back disk state.

## Acceptance cases

F1: fresh Set A, project P, two warped audio clips referencing valid PCM WAV X,
and compatible PCM WAV Y variants at the same sample rate. X has 100,000 frames;
Y variants have 80,000/100,000/120,000 frames. Give both clips distinguishable
nondefault Warp Markers and valid nondefault clip properties; record their
pre-operation marker/property state. Chosen loop/extents must fit even the shorter
replacement so this test does not rely on an unknown out-of-source clamp.
The [declarative fixture](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/project-media/fixtures.json)
defines mandatory nonempty marker/state controls. F2: source Set S with one audio,
one MIDI, one return and a nested group, distinguishable clips/devices/automation.
F3: projects P/Q with test asset X inside P but used by Q only; project-owned
and external samples from each selectable location class. Operations use copies.
Choose an undoable documentary action with an independently known transaction
boundary for history cases; this page does not define an edit's transaction.

| PMW-001 | 001 | Positive | Create A, then open named S. | Named current Set changes; content according to its existing format contract. |
| PMW-002 | 002 | Positive | Save A, then Save As to distinct test name. | Named destination receives saved Set; byte format out of this case. |
| PMW-003 | 002 | Boundary | Save a Copy to distinct destination. | New named copy exists; current identity U. |
| PMW-004 | 003 | History | Perform three known undoable actions; choose earliest history action. | Later actions dim/undo; newest-to-oldest ordering. |
| PMW-005 | 003 | History | Select a later dimmed action. | Relevant undone action sequence reapplied; edit grouping independently controlled. |
| PMW-006 | 004 | Teardown/reopen | Close/reopen saved A. | Fresh history; initial opening not undoable. |
| PMW-007 | 005 | Positive/negative | Drag S into target Set drop area. | Import non-return tracks and described content; source return excluded; remapping U. |
| PMW-008 | 006 | Selection | Unfold S/nested group and import one track, then one Session clip. | Only chosen imported object scope; merge remapping/extra context U. |
| PMW-009 | 007 | Positive | Export two selected Session clips to test user folder. | New named Set for selection; exact extra contents U. |
| PMW-010 | 008 | State | Save a distinguishable default, create new Set. | Configured default state represented; exact coverage of every device/plugin setting U. |
| PMW-011 | 009 | State | Save/load named template. | Templates listing and configured untitled instance. |
| PMW-012 | 010 | References | View A's X references and expand usage. | Listed reference shows both clip usages and location class. |
| PMW-013 | 011 | Equal-length boundary | Replace X with equal-length Y in reference list. | Both references redirect; Warp Markers retained. |
| PMW-014 | 011 | Longer boundary | Replace X with longer Y. | Both references redirect; Warp Markers retained. |
| PMW-015 | 011 | Shorter boundary | Replace X with shorter Y. | Warp Markers discarded; other applicable clip properties retained. |
| PMW-016 | 012 | External edit | Engage Edit; keep X duration unchanged. | Offline while engaged; markers retained on documented return; exact refresh timing U. |
| PMW-017 | 012 | Changed duration | External edit changes X duration. | Old Warp Markers not retained; replacement/default marker state U. |
| PMW-018 | 013 | Project boundary | Save fresh A outside projects, then Save As inside existing P. | New project versus shared project; no automatic external collection asserted. |
| PMW-019 | 014 | Version boundary | Open valid older-major Set, attempt overwrite. | Save As required; unsupported file versions remain separate. |
| PMW-020 | 015 | Missing input | Make X unavailable before loading A. | Affected usages offline; missing sample contributes silence; unrelated/tail output ungraded. |
| PMW-021 | 016 | Reassignment | Use different valid audio Y to repair missing X. | Manual reassignment accepted without original-identity requirement. |
| PMW-022 | 017 | No candidate | Search controlled empty folder only. | Missing reference unresolved. |
| PMW-023 | 017 | One candidate | Supply exactly one matching candidate by independently established search criteria. | Candidate accepted; matching algorithm outside comparator. |
| PMW-024 | 017 | Several candidates | Supply two matching candidates under same controlled criteria. | User candidate selection offered; ordering U. |
| PMW-025 | 018 | Collection | Select one external-location class, Collect and Save. | Selected dependencies copied/referenced within P; omitted classes not graded. |
| PMW-026 | 019 | Always/Never | Export sample-bearing preset under each preference. | Copy versus original-reference behavior; exact destination layout U. |
| PMW-027 | 019 | Ask/Copy | Confirm Copy, then confirm item filename. | Dependent copying follows filename confirmation. |
| PMW-028 | 019 | Cancellation | Choose Cancel at Ask prompt. | Export process quit; atomicity/partial filesystem state U. |
| PMW-029 | 020 | Cross-project boundary | Inspect X in P used only by Q. | X considered unused in P despite Q usage. |
| PMW-030 | 021 | Pack | Pack P containing uncollected external X; install to fresh location. | Packed project restored; external X not automatically collected; original P remains. |
| PMW-031 | 022 | Malformed | Corrupt ALS/ALP/media or ambiguous candidate identity. | U beyond existing narrower format refusals. |
| PMW-032 | 022 | Failure | Deny destination access or exhaust space during collect/save/pack. | U diagnostics, partial output, rollback and recovery. |
| PMW-033 | 022 | Cancellation | Cancel collect/pack/search/external editor mid-operation. | U accepted cancellation points and preserved state. |
| PMW-034 | 022 | Undo/teardown | Undo file replacement, or close/replace Set mid-write. | U undo grouping, save prompts, reference restoration and cleanup. |

All 34 cases are unexecuted. PMW-001–030 have bounded documented-domain criteria,
with additional ungraded limits as shown; PMW-031–034 are wholly ungraded. Exact
12.4.3 behavior is U throughout. There is no graded byte/audio equality test.

## Open questions

[Q-027](../questions.md#q-027-whole-product-specification-evidence-and-version-coverage)
owns manual/build applicability. Narrower unresolved questions: copy versus
active-document identity; ID/routing/automation remapping during merge; nearly
equal replacement duration; search criteria/ranking; collection collisions and
location naming; missing plugin/Max dependencies; Save As/version migration;
ALP format/install boundaries; cancel/failure atomicity, rollback/recovery,
permission handling, undo grouping and external edit refresh/reclamation.

Audio/video/MIDI render/export settings, decoding cache/ASD behavior, codec
support, destructive clip editing, file-format bytes and filesystem-watch
latency remain separate unclosed F-07 obligations. The manual has relevant
sections; citing the whole chapter does not specify those omitted contracts.
